critical_issues: CRITICAL (HONESTY, item #4 — the single most dangerous hole): matmul_f32_tiled.axc declares `@strategy { tile_m: ?[1,2,4], tile_n: ?[1,2,4] }` but the KERNEL BODY NEVER REFERENCES tile_m OR tile_n. Verified: grep of examples/matmul_f32_tiled.axc shows tile_m/tile_n appear ONLY in the @strategy line and comments; the body unconditionally computes ONE output element per invocation (let i = gid(0); row=i/n; col=i-row*n; scalar k-loop). Therefore pinning {tile_m:1, tile_n:1} does NOT produce a '1x1 tiled' matmul — it produces a NAIVE SCALAR GEMM, and pinning 2 or 4 would produce BYTE-IDENTICAL SPIR-V (the holes are dead). The spec's own prose ('tile_m=1,tile_n=1 is the first candidate = one (row,col) element per invocation') confirms this but the design_md_additions and AT-1576 present effective_tflops as 'AXIOM-Compute matmul performance' / 'first measured kernel-only TFLOPS' for a GEMM. Reporting a naive-uncoalesced-scalar-GEMM number under the banner 'effective TFLOPS' is exactly the reward-hacking-style misrepresentation the project thesis exists to prevent. The number is REAL but the LABEL is misleading. REQUIRED FIX: the bench's printed line AND design_md_additions MUST state verbatim that this is a NAIVE non-tiled scalar f32 GEMM (one output element per invocation, uncoalesced B access), that the @strategy tile holes are presently INERT (not wired into the kernel body), and that the % of cuBLAS is expected to be a low single-digit fraction. Do NOT call it 'AXIOM-Compute's matmul' without the 'naive/un-tiled, harness-validation-only' qualifier. M3.4 is where a real tiled/coopmat kernel produces a comparable number.

CRITICAL (TIMING SEMANTICS, item #1): TOP_OF_PIPE -> BOTTOM_OF_PIPE is the WRONG pair for an honest KERNEL-ONLY duration. Per Vulkan, vkCmdWriteTimestamp(TOP_OF_PIPE, q0) writes when the command REACHES the top of the pipe (i.e. as soon as the prior commands' top-of-pipe is reached — effectively at the start of the CB), and vkCmdWriteTimestamp(BOTTOM_OF_PIPE, q1) writes when ALL prior commands (the dispatch) have completed. So TOP->BOTTOM actually OVER-counts relative to pure compute-shader execution (it includes the pipeline drain / latency from the queue picking up the CB through full completion), NOT under-counts — but more importantly the design DOC (resident.rs module header lines 22-26) and the spec describe it as 'kernel-only', which is an approximation, not an identity. This is acceptable as a measurement ONLY if it is HONESTLY labeled as 'submit-to-completion GPU timestamp delta (includes pipeline latency), not isolated ALU time'. The pair choice (TOP at q0 before bind, BOTTOM at q1 after dispatch) is the conventional and DEFENSIBLE choice and is fine — but the prose claiming it is 'kernel-only' must be softened to 'GPU-side dispatch duration (timestamp TOP-of-pipe to BOTTOM-of-pipe spanning the single dispatch)'. Acceptable with a doc fix; flagged because the milestone's entire value proposition rests on the timing claim being honest.

CRITICAL (API SAFETY GAP, item #4b): dispatch_resident as specified does NOT call validate_request / does NOT check cfg.workgroups against max_compute_work_group_count(). Verified: the workgroup-limit guard (DispatchError::WorkgroupCountExceedsDeviceLimit at dispatch.rs:56/87) is invoked ONLY inside dispatch_handle (context.rs:909). The spec pushes the wg_x guard into the BENCH code only ('the bench must pick the largest pow2...'). Any OTHER caller of the new public dispatch_resident with an out-of-range workgroups triggers a raw driver validation error or hang. REQUIRED FIX: dispatch_resident MUST call validate_request (or an equivalent max_compute_work_group_count check) on cfg.workgroups and return WorkgroupCountExceedsDeviceLimit — the guard belongs in the library method, not duplicated in every caller. This also subsumes the bench's manual guard.
warnings: WARNING (item #1, warmup): The METHOD is self-contained per call (correct without warmup), but on a timestamp-capable GPU the FIRST dispatch pays pipeline warm-up + clock ramp + first-touch page-in. The architect's own open_question recommends 2 warm-up + min-of-N; this MUST be a hard requirement in the bench AND in AT-1530, not a 'RECOMMENDED'. Without enforced warmup-discard the reported TFLOPS is inflated-low (slower) and the AT-1530 'kernel_ns < host roundtrip' assertion could even FLAKE if the first-iter outlier is the one measured. Make warmup-discard mandatory and assert on min/median of post-warmup samples.

WARNING (item #1, fallback labeling): The CpuFenceWall fallback returns submit+fence-wall ns under the SAME ResidentDispatchTiming.kernel_ns field as the GpuTimestamp path. On Lavapipe this number INCLUDES submit latency, fence scheduling, and driver overhead — it is NOT a kernel time. The enum field timing_source DOES distinguish them (good), but the bench's printed 'X TFLOPS' line and AT-1530 must REFUSE to present a CpuFenceWall number as a kernel-only TFLOPS figure (or must print 'CpuFenceWall — NOT kernel-only, scheduling-inclusive' next to it). AT-1530 already relaxes the smaller-than assertion on Lavapipe; extend that to the PRINTED label so a Lavapipe CI number is never quoted as a GPU kernel time.

WARNING (item #2, drop/leak on upload failure): The spec relies on a 'mirror the inspect_err cleanup pattern' for partial-allocation cleanup inside upload_resident, but the existing ResidentBuffers::Drop (resident.rs:127-162) ONLY frees a FULLY-built struct. The upload path creates a transient upload staging buffer + transient upload command pool/CB that are NOT fields of ResidentBuffers and are freed manually mid-function. If allocation of the descriptor pool / reusable CB / fence / query pool fails AFTER the transient upload objects are freed but BEFORE ResidentBuffers is constructed, every already-created persistent object (device-local buffers, descriptor pool, staging buffers) must be hand-freed — there is no RAII guard. This is a real leak surface. REQUIRE: the Coder either (a) builds ResidentBuffers incrementally into an Option and lets Drop handle teardown, or (b) writes an explicit ordered cleanup on every early-return Err. QA must read the diff for EACH early return.

WARNING (item #3, query pool WAIT vs fence redundancy is fine, but stale-result hazard on the CpuFenceWall->later-GpuTimestamp transition): use_gpu_ts is snapshotted at upload from timestamp_valid_bits/period (immutable), so a single ResidentBuffers never flips paths mid-life — good, no stale hazard. However the query pool is created UNCONDITIONALLY (count=2) even when use_gpu_ts is false; on a device with timestampValidBits==0, vkCmdWriteTimestamp must NOT be recorded (spec: timestamp writes require timestampValidBits>0 on the queue family). The spec correctly gates cmd_write_timestamp behind use_gpu_ts (steps 2/5 'if use_gpu_ts') — VERIFY the Coder also SKIPS creating the query pool OR at minimum never records into it when valid_bits==0. Creating an unused query pool is harmless; recording a timestamp on a 0-valid-bits queue is a validation error.

WARNING (item #5): prepare_kernel_checked is ADDITIVE and does NOT retrofit the existing prepare_kernel callers (the bench's own prepare_kernel call at resident_matmul.rs:111/177 stays unchecked unless the Coder switches it). This RELOCATES the guard into a new opt-in method rather than CLOSING the hole for existing callers. It satisfies the M3.1 carry-forward intent ONLY for callers that adopt the new method. The spec must (a) explicitly switch the bench + the new tests to prepare_kernel_checked, and (b) acknowledge that production code paths still using prepare_kernel remain unprotected by design. Honest, but the milestone summary should not claim the preflight gap is 'closed' — it is 'closeable opt-in'.

WARNING (item #2, descriptor independence): the open_question's decision to give ResidentBuffers its OWN descriptor pool+set (independent of handle.inner.descriptor_set) is the CORRECT no-aliasing design and avoids mutating the handle's set. Confirmed safe. BUT dispatch_resident MUST bind resident.descriptor_set, NOT handle.inner.descriptor_set. The technical_spec step 3 says 'cmd_bind_descriptor_sets(..., [ds], [])' where ds = resident's set — VERIFY the Coder binds the RESIDENT set; binding handle.inner.descriptor_set would read the handle's (unwritten) buffer pool and silently compute garbage. This is a high-value QA check.
principle_violations: VIOLATION (anti-pattern #4 'No feature without a test' / project thesis on verifiable intent): presenting a naive scalar GEMM's throughput as 'matmul TFLOPS' with inert @strategy tile holes is precisely the implicit-intent / unverified-claim failure mode the project is built to avoid. Not a code-UB violation, but a thesis-level honesty violation — fixed by mandatory truthful labeling (see CRITICAL #1).
spirv_concerns: No new SPIR-V capabilities/extensions (spirv_capabilities_required=[], confirmed). The resident path reuses the already-validated pipeline from prepare_kernel; no codegen surface changes. spirv-val output is unchanged. No SPIR-V concern.
vendor_concerns: subgroup_size()==32 hard gate in preflight_kernel_support correctly SKIPS (CoopMatUnsupported) on AMD wave64/Intel-variable rather than miscompiling — verified against the existing context.rs subgroup_size query and the coopmat path. Good. The f32 naive matmul path has no subgroup dependency and runs on all vendors (including Lavapipe via CpuFenceWall). No new vendor hazard, provided the timestamp-write gating (valid_bits>0) is honored on devices that report 0 (Lavapipe).
timestampPeriod==0 OR timestampValidBits==0 fallback to CpuFenceWall is the right portability choice; just ensure no vkCmdWriteTimestamp is recorded on those devices (see WARNING above).
missing_tests: MUST TEST: dispatch_resident rejects an out-of-range cfg.workgroups with WorkgroupCountExceedsDeviceLimit (once the library guard is added per CRITICAL #4b) — pure/Lavapipe testable without a huge dispatch.

MUST TEST: dispatch_resident binds the RESIDENT descriptor set, proven by AT-1570 output-equality vs dispatch_handle (already planned) — but explicitly add an assertion/comment that a regression to handle.inner.descriptor_set would FAIL AT-1570 (it would read unwritten buffers). Keep AT-1570 as the guard.

MUST TEST: upload_resident partial-failure cleanup does not leak (hard to trigger on a real GPU; at minimum add a #[allow]-documented note + a unit test of the cleanup ordering if a fault-injection seam exists). QA must read each early-return Err in the diff.

MUST TEST (labeling): a test or doc-assertion that the matmul_tflops bench's printed string contains the words 'naive'/'un-tiled' (or equivalent) so the honesty label cannot silently regress. The number's correctness is already covered by AT-1576; the LABEL needs a guard too.

Already-planned coverage is otherwise adequate: AT-1573 (pure timing-source selection), AT-1571 (CB/fence/query reuse), AT-1572 (Lever A skip), AT-1575 (panic->error), AT-1530/1531 (GPU), AT-1577 (regression+clippy). Anti-pattern #9 honored (real GPU / Lavapipe fallback).
questions_for_architect: Will dispatch_resident call validate_request (or check max_compute_work_group_count) internally, so the public API is safe for non-bench callers? (Currently the guard lives only in dispatch_handle and the spec pushes it to bench code.)

Will the bench's printed line and design_md_additions be rewritten to state explicitly that matmul_f32_tiled tile=1 is a NAIVE non-tiled scalar GEMM with INERT tile holes, expected to be a low single-digit % of cuBLAS? (Required to clear CRITICAL #1.)

Will the module-doc / spec prose stop calling the TOP->BOTTOM timestamp delta 'kernel-only' and instead call it 'GPU dispatch duration (submit-to-completion timestamp span, includes pipeline latency)'? (Required to clear CRITICAL #1 timing claim.)
Will warmup-discard (>=2 untimed dispatches, report min/median of N) be MANDATORY in the bench and AT-1530, not 'recommended'?

Will the bench + new tests actually SWITCH to prepare_kernel_checked (so the carry-forward gap is exercised), and does the milestone summary stop claiming the gap is 'closed' for unchanged prepare_kernel callers?
summary: NEEDS_REVISION. The structural plan is sound — additive API, correct independent descriptor set (no aliasing), HN-6 query reset ordering, queue_submit_lock preserved, panic->typed-error well specified, 50 GB cap respected, anti-pattern #9 honored — and most of items 2/3/5/6/7 pass with named QA checks. BUT three honesty/correctness holes block approval: (1) item #4 — matmul_f32_tiled's tile_m/tile_n holes are DEAD (never referenced in the kernel body, verified), so {tile_m:1,tile_n:1} yields a NAIVE scalar GEMM whose 'effective TFLOPS' would be presented as AXIOM-Compute matmul performance; this MUST be relabeled as a naive/un-tiled harness-validation number with inert tile holes. (2) item #1 — calling the TOP->BOTTOM timestamp delta 'kernel-only' overstates it (it is submit-to-completion / includes pipeline latency); the doc must say so, the CpuFenceWall fallback must never be quoted as a kernel time, and warmup-discard must be mandatory. (3) item #4b — dispatch_resident as specified never validates cfg.workgroups against max_compute_work_group_count, so the new public method can drive an out-of-range dispatch into a validation error/hang for any non-bench caller; the guard must move into the library method. Plus a real leak surface on partial upload_resident failure (no RAII for transient/persistent objects mid-construction). Fix the labeling (CRITICAL #1), the timing prose + warmup + fallback labeling (CRITICAL #1 timing), the workgroup guard (CRITICAL #4b), and specify the upload cleanup ordering, then this is approvable.
